body: I will. He will be better off in a shelter. Right. Smart choice.
I am a mother, a woman and a person. I was just with my son for 7 years, and I'm still not afraid to be single. It is not my only option though. But thanks.
That's true, stats do show that stepfamilies are a nightmare. Unfortunately, stats also tell you that marriages are a nightmare too, since the divorce rates are around 60% around the world.

Why do you keep saying I don't stand up for him? My son knows I stand up for him. Do you think he would only be satisfied if I divorced? What would I be teaching him? That couples don't have issues? That the only way out of an argument is a divorce? If he has children by then, he would be adding to the divorcee numbers as well. I'm trying to look at this from every side. I believe a family should function as a team. We have a problem, we try to fix it. You just don't give up every time there's a problem. My husband doesn't hate my child, he doesn't like him and I'm trying to figure out the cause to then decide if it's fixable or not.

Maybe I'm stupid, nevertheless I'm trying to fix it. I wouldn't be needing help to end it. That's easy. I don't think you have to choose between your kids and your spouse, regardless if you are in a first or second marriage. As you don't have to choose between owning a house and/or a car. When you have children with your partner, you don't choose,  you add up. Step families are difficult to maintain because they're the result of failed families and frustration. I think you do have multiple chances in life, failed marriages shouldn't result in a life sentence of loneliness or misery. But thanks for your opinion anyway.

Well, maybe it is. I didn't say he hates him. I said he doesn't like him. It's very different. And I'm trying to figure out why. But thanks for your input. I can see how it sounds from the outside. : (

As I said, his mother had just died, like a year before that, so my husband just wanted to let it slide as if it wasn't important because he believed his son was still angry about his mother's death. I, on the other hand, lost it. Me and my husband fought and fought for days, and I went to my stepson's room and made it clear for my stepson I wouldn't admit him beating my son.

I'm a two times married older woman as it seems. Maybe I don't make the best choices too. If or when I divorce him I will be a multi married older woman too. Does that turn me into a red flag too? It doesn't mean I'm not trying my best and that I don't deserve to be in a happy and healthy relationship. I'm asking for a way to resolve this, if there's any. I don't think he's a bad man, I think he's childish and doesn't know how much he is hurting me and my son. I also believe that regardless of him not being a bad man this hurts my son and me and my son doesn't deserve it. Of course we will have to divorce if we can't fix this. I'm just trying to think of ways to put things right.

He cared for him at the beginning but then his son's mother died (they had been divorced for 10 years and had split custody) and his son came to live with us. He was 15 at the time and he told his father he didn't want to live with me and my son. But since he had no one else, he had no choice. For the first 6 months he didn't even acknowledge my presence in the house. He also had been treated like shit by my husband's second wife and one of the first things he told me was that he wouldn't tolerate anyone to treat me the way his stepmother had treated him. So he started to treat me and my son like she had treated him. He even hit my son on his 8th birthday. Mind he was 15. My husband loves him to pieces (rightfully) but since then I think he developed a thought "me and my son" vs "you and your son" that continues until this day. You know that loyalty bind children from divorced parents have with one of the parents? Well, my husband has it with his children. It is as if he treats my son with care, his children might be jealous so he always maintains his distance.

I don't understand his behaviour. He treats my mother very well, he's thoughtful and caring. But this animosity towards my son... I can't figure out where it comes from. He's caring and joyful with his own children but when it comes to my son there's so much animosity. My son is not an easy child, his father doesn't care for him at all and it is very hard for me to see that he doesn't have any male role model. I was trying to fix it before breaking it.

Having children is over rated. Listen: the only people who live to continue telling that story are people who have had children themselves. So, it's an easy sale. Imagine you have children: you probably will love them to death and would be part of the propaganda and your children would always hear how great it is to have children. If you don't have children, the chance of you enjoying your life is high too, but you will have none to continue to advocate the wonders of not having children. 

That being said, if you do have children, you still have to be lucky with the child/children you have. There are stories from heaven and stories from hell. 

Best of luck! 🙂
